$sources: The species: Phyllostachys aureosulcata McClure, huang cao zhu, yellow-groove bamboo: culms 3-9 m, 1-4 cm across, green with a yellow groove (sulcus) above each branch, the lower internodes sometimes zigzag; branches two at a node; leaves 7-15 cm by 1-1.5 cm (Flora of China (Wu Zhengyi, P. H. Raven and Hong Deyuan, eds., Science Press and Missouri Botanical Garden, 1994-2013), vol. 22, Poaceae, Bambusoideae).

Culm habit, internodes, branching and sprays: the as-built museum's grove (windows/Source/MuseeVision/Nature/MuseeTree.cpp, GrowBamboo): culms 4.7-6.1 m, 22-32 mm radius at the foot, leaves 10-17 cm, 12-15 % as wide as long.
name: Phyllostachys aureosulcata
note: Each plant is one culm, standing at its point in the grove as the Chenghuai sheet plots them (the as-built culm points). Its culm radius is the species' 1-4 cm across. The museum shows it in early summer, Mangzhong to Xiazhi (June).
